name: Mining & Metals
one_liner: Extracting and processing minerals and metals, a price-taking, capital-intensive business where position on the cost curve determines survival.
how_it_makes_money: Miners sell ore, concentrates or refined metal at global commodity prices, often benchmarked to exchanges such as the LME. Profits depend on the gap between price and all-in cost per unit, so low-cost, long-life assets are the prize. Some companies also earn processing, smelting or royalty and streaming income.
revenue_formula: Revenue = ore mined × grade × recovery rate × realized metal price
Revenue = tonnes sold × price per tonne (bulk commodities like iron ore and coal)
cost_structure: Energy and fuel: diesel for haul trucks and power for processing
Equipment and maintenance: haul trucks, shovels, mills
Sustaining and growth capex, plus closure and reclamation
margins: Very cyclical: low-cost producers can earn strong margins at the top of the cycle while high-cost mines lose money in downturns. Ore grade, cost curve position, jurisdiction and scale drive the spread.

key_metrics.name: All-in sustaining cost (AISC)
key_metrics.what: Full cost per ounce or pound to maintain output, the standard gold and copper benchmark.

key_metrics.name: Cost curve position (quartile)
key_metrics.what: Where a mine sits versus global supply; first-quartile assets survive downturns.

key_metrics.name: Ore grade
key_metrics.what: Metal content per tonne of ore; declining grades raise costs.

key_metrics.name: Recovery rate
key_metrics.what: Share of metal extracted from ore during processing.

key_metrics.name: Reserve life (years)
key_metrics.what: How long current reserves last at present production.

key_metrics.name: Strip ratio
key_metrics.what: Waste moved per tonne of ore, a key driver of open-pit costs.

trends: Energy transition demand for copper, lithium, nickel and rare earths
Critical minerals policy and supply chain security, especially reducing reliance on China
Declining ore grades and long permitting times constraining new supply
Large-scale consolidation as majors buy copper exposure
Automation and electrification of mine fleets
ESG, community relations and tailings safety as license to operate
